note: Adapted from the description of the new genus and species by Scheffrahn & Carrijo (2023), in English; only the worker is described (monotypic), and the alate is explicitly recorded as unknown; the measurements are taken from Table 1 (10 workers, the original gives only ranges and means).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule and antennae pale yellow; head with about 50 longer setae (0.1 mm) and a few short setae; in lateral view the dorsal surface of the head capsule slightly convex, postclypeus moderately raised. Antennae 14-segmented (segment order 2>3≈4<5). Pronotum with about 20 long setae, mainly concentrated at the margins, plus a few short hairs. Apical tooth of the mandibles very prominent; left mandible M1 triangular, shorter than the apical tooth; premolar process longer than M3. Right mandible apical tooth as long as that of the left but narrower, M1 and M2 equal in length. Fore tibia moderately inflated, with about ten or more stout posterior setae on its posterior half, and both long slender and shorter setae on the lateral and anterior surfaces. Digestive tract: crop large; midgut semicircular; mixed segment with a prominent spherical midgut tongue; first proctodeal segment (P1) reaching its greatest diameter before P2, enteric valve seat slightly trilobed; third proctodeal segment (P3) with a long tubular extension to the main reservoir, narrowing again towards P4. Enteric valve armature cuticle unclerotized, forming 6 rectangular pads, each with about 100 scales; scales near the P1 end nearly rectangular, each with 5—10 ridges; scales of the distal third without ridges, more scale-like and with long fringes. Measurements (mm, 10 workers): head length to the lateral mandibular bases 0.70—0.77; maximum head width 0.82—0.93; hind tibia length 0.67—0.77; postclypeus length 0.18—0.25, width 0.39—0.44; fore tibia length 0.53—0.67, width 0.12—0.18; fore tibia width/length ratio 0.21—0.30.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The combination of unclerotized rectangular pads on the enteric valve armature, a tubular extension of the enteric valve seat and a prominent spherical midgut tongue is unique to C. pax among the genera of Apicotermitinae. Only the worker is known, the alate unknown; so far known only from the northern range of Trinidad, workers collected under stones, the gut contents soil organic matter.
